# Job #56: STM32H743 AIO Nano FC + 4-in-1 ESC
## System Architecture, Loss Model, Thermal Budget, and DShot DMA Allocation

---

## 0. Assumptions and Scope

**Architecture.** The STM32H743 is the flight controller. It does not commutate the motors. The 48 kHz PWM is generated by four dedicated ESC MCUs (AT32F421 running AM32 is assumed), which receive bidirectional DShot600 from the H743. A single-MCU FOC architecture on the H743 would need a completely different timer plan and is not covered here.

**Definition of "80 A burst".** This is taken as **80 A phase current per motor, all four motors at once**, on 6S (25.2 V full charge).

**Form factor.** "Nano" is taken as 25.5 × 25.5 mm (20 × 20 mm mounting). A smaller board makes the thermal result below worse.

**Reference MOSFET.** No part number was specified, so all numbers use a representative 40 V, 3.3 × 3.3 mm PQFN. **Substitute your selected part's datasheet values before release.**

| Parameter | Symbol | Value |
|---|---|---|
| On-resistance, 25 °C, V_GS = 10 V (max) | R_DS(on),25 | 1.2 mΩ |
| R_DS(on) tempco (normalized) | α | 0.006 /K |
| Gate–drain charge | Q_gd | 6 nC |
| Post-threshold gate–source charge | Q_gs2 | 3 nC |
| Total gate charge | Q_g | 30 nC |
| Reverse-recovery charge | Q_rr | 25 nC |
| Output charge | Q_oss | 20 nC |
| Miller plateau voltage | V_pl | 3.0 V |
| Body-diode forward voltage | V_f | 0.8 V |
| Junction-to-case thermal resistance | R_θJC | 1.5 K/W |
| Internal gate resistance | R_g,int | 1.0 Ω |

**Headline result (derived in §3).** 80 A on all four channels at once is **not a sustainable operating point** on a nano board. Total dissipation is about 125 W, and the board reaches its thermal limit in roughly **2 seconds**. The firmware limits in §3.4 are mandatory, not optional.
